rawOutput.title: Use the Product Rule Independently
rawOutput.rationale: This is a conceptual learning and problem-solving plan. It begins with one complete example because the product rule is new, then moves through guided use, independent practice, and mixed verification. Each 15-minute session keeps one action prominent and uses attempts to determine what support is needed.

sessions.title: Understand the Product Rule
sessions.objective: Recognize when the product rule applies and explain its structure through a complete example.
sessions.amountLabel: Product rule meaning, formula, and one worked derivative
contentTargets: The product rule as the derivative of two multiplied functions
Applying the rule in one complete example using familiar power-rule derivatives
completionEvidence: Explain why differentiating each factor and multiplying the results is incorrect
Construct the derivative of one product by identifying both factors and applying the formula

sessions.title: Apply the Rule With Guidance
sessions.objective: Use the product rule step by step on a similar expression.
contentTargets: Choosing the two factors and their derivatives
Substituting correctly into the product-rule structure
completionEvidence: Solve one polynomial product derivative with step-by-step prompts
Solve a second derivative with prompts removed after setup

sessions.title: Use the Rule Independently
sessions.objective: Differentiate products without a supplied setup and repair any errors.
sessions.amountLabel: Two independent product-rule problems with error repair
contentTargets: Independent product-rule setup and calculation
Checking factor order, derivatives, and algebra
completionEvidence: Solve two product-rule derivatives without setup prompts
Explain and correct any error found by checking each term against the rule

sessions.title: Verify Flexible Use
sessions.objective: Distinguish product-rule problems from power-rule problems and apply the correct procedure.
sessions.amountLabel: Four-item mixed check covering rule selection and independent use
contentTargets: Selecting between the power rule and product rule
Independent product-rule use in mixed practice
completionEvidence: Classify four expressions by the differentiation rule required
Solve the product-rule items independently and justify the setup

activities.label: Product rule model
activities.title: How the product rule works
activities.body: Review the rule and notice the two paired terms. Then move to the check.

essentialIdeas: The derivative of a product is found by taking the derivative of one factor while keeping the other factor unchanged, then adding the reverse pairing.

activities.label: Say it in your own words
activities.title: Explain the rule simply
activities.body: Write the rule in your own words. Keep it brief and specific.
activities.concept: State the product rule in plain language.
activities.correctAnswer: Take the derivative of the first factor and keep the second factor, then add the first factor times the derivative of the second factor.
activities.feedback: A complete answer names both terms and shows that one factor stays unchanged in each term.

activities.label: Fix the setup
activities.title: Correct the two terms
activities.body: Suppose a product was set up with both factors changing in both terms. Fix the rule.
activities.misconceptionSummary: Both factors change in both terms of the product rule.
activities.concept: Repair the product-rule setup so each term changes only one factor.
activities.correctAnswer: One term uses the derivative of the first factor times the second factor unchanged; the other term uses the first factor unchanged times the derivative of the second factor.
activities.feedback: The key correction is that each product-rule term changes only one factor. The other factor stays the same in that term.

activities.label: Explain it again
activities.title: Restate the rule clearly
activities.body: Say the rule again after the repair. Keep it in plain language.
activities.concept: Restate the product rule after repair.
activities.correctAnswer: For a product, differentiate the first factor and keep the second, then add the first factor times the derivative of the second.
activities.feedback: This should now be clean, complete, and free of the earlier mixup.

items.essentialIdea: The product rule says the derivative of two multiplied functions equals f'g + fg'.

check.title: Differentiate a product
check.prompt: How do you differentiate the product of two functions f(x) and g(x)?
check.referenceAnswer: Differentiate each function once and add the cross terms: (fg)' = f'g + fg'.
check.feedback: The derivative is not the product of the derivatives; each factor contributes one term.

recognitionCheck.title: Product rule form

check.feedback: The derivative is not the product of the derivatives; each factor contributes one term.

recognitionCheck.title: Product rule form
recognitionCheck.prompt: Which expression correctly gives the derivative of f(x)g(x)?
recognitionCheck.feedback: The product rule adds one term from differentiating each factor.
